import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

`make test-e2e` runs Go suites against a **live local stack** over HTTP, with a real JWT login and real Postgres rows, no mocks. Some suites call a real LLM, so every test agent gets a **hard-fail daily budget** from a fixed set of named agents. If a cap is hit the test fails on purpose: the guard works, and a bad loop cannot run up a bill. A second tier replays recorded LLM and connector responses, so CI needs no provider key and spends nothing.

## Run the suites

```bash
make dev-infra   # Postgres + Redis + MinIO (once)
make run-api     # control plane on :8080 (terminal 1)

export PAL_E2E_API_URL=http://localhost:8080
make test-e2e    # terminal 2
```

The target runs `make e2e-lint`, then the `e2e/runtime`, `e2e/quickstart`, `e2e/examples` and `e2e/deploy` suites. They are Go with build tag `e2e`, in standalone modules, so plain `go test ./...` never runs them. `make test-e2e-llm` is an alias. It targets the single-tier topology (stub scheduler, no KVM needed), and the quickstart suite needs an LLM provider configured for the dev tenant.

On a two-tier stack (`PAL_SCHEDULER_GRPC_ADDR` plus a Docker-backend runtime-manager), set `PAL_E2E_IMAGE_DIGEST` to a locally pullable image. With the placeholder default, schedule returns 500.

If the stack is down, every test **fails**, so `make test-e2e` exits non-zero and you know nothing ran. `E2E_ALLOW_SKIP=1` turns that into a skip with exit 0. A reachable API with wrong credentials is always a failure.

<Aside type="danger">
Never point the suites at a stack with real tenant data: they delete every agent named `e2e-*` in the logged-in tenant.
</Aside>

| Suite | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `e2e/runtime` | `/v1/runtime/*` control path: auth gates, schedule (201 + vm_id), tenant-scoped list, detail and audit, logs SSE, terminate, quota 402. |
| `e2e/quickstart` | The `examples/quickstart/` agents: create from `spec.json`, post `run.json`, poll to `succeeded`, assert an output shape. incident-summarizer also issues and verifies a receipt. Real LLM calls. |
| `e2e/examples` | The fixture-tier example flows (digest, Telegram, voice). Needs the fixture stack that `make test-e2e-examples` builds. |
| `e2e/deploy` | The deploy CLI against a control plane (the `deploy-cli` CI job). |

## Environment

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PAL_E2E_API_URL` | `http://localhost:8080` | Target API. Always set it explicitly. |
| `PAL_API_URL` | unset | Alias, used only when the canonical variable is unset |
| `PAL_E2E_EMAIL` | `admin@lantern.dev` | Login email (seeded dev user) |
| `PAL_E2E_PASSWORD` | `lantern` | Login password |
| `PAL_E2E_IMAGE_DIGEST` | placeholder digest | Image to schedule in the runtime suite; needed on two-tier stacks |
| `E2E_ALLOW_SKIP` | unset | `1` turns a down stack into a skip |

## Spend policy

Enforced by `e2e/internal/e2ekit`, the only way a suite creates agents or posts runs.

- **Reserved names.** Agent names must be one of 8: `e2e-quickstart`, `e2e-support`, `e2e-pr-triage`, `e2e-incident`, `e2e-digest`, `e2e-analyst`, `e2e-assistant`, `e2e-voice`. At most 8 `e2e-*` agents exist at once.
- **Budget first.** Each agent gets a hard-fail budget before any run: `maxCostUsdPerDay` 0.50, `maxRunsPerDay` 15, `hardFail` true. The kit reads it back and fails the test if it is absent.
- **Cheapest model.** The model is pinned to `reasoning-small` if Anthropic is configured, else `chat-small`, else `fast` (env-configured keys). Never a large model.
- **No search.** `web_search` is stripped from every spec except `e2e-assistant`.
- **A 402 fails the test** with `e2e daily budget exhausted for <name> (cap working; rerun after local midnight)`.
- **Tenant cap untouched.** `make e2e-lint` fails the build if anything under `e2e/` references `/v1/budgets/tenant`.

The quickstart suite posts 3 runs per invocation against one slot, and the cap is 15 runs a day, so expect about 5 full runs per day.

## Cleanup

Tests delete their agents with `t.Cleanup`, and the runtime suite terminates its VMs and restores its temporary quota row even when assertions fail. The quickstart suite also sweeps leftover `e2e-*` agents in `TestMain`.

After an interrupted run, recover manually. `make e2e-clean` runs `go run ./cmd/sweep` in `e2e/internal/e2ekit`, lists `GET /v1/agents`, and issues `DELETE /v1/agents/{name}` for every agent whose name starts with `e2e-`. Nothing else is deleted, and failures are printed, never fatal. Use it when the kit refuses to create an agent because 8 `e2e-*` agents already exist.

```bash
PAL_E2E_API_URL=http://localhost:8080 make e2e-clean
```

## Fixture LLM tier

`llm-replay` is a small standard-library server that speaks the OpenAI chat-completions and Anthropic messages wire formats (JSON and SSE streaming, text and tool calls). Setting `PAL_LLM_BASEURL_OPENAI` and/or `PAL_LLM_BASEURL_ANTHROPIC` sends every control-plane provider call there instead of the real API. CI and kiosk mode use it so answers are identical every time and need no key. Token usage is still reported, so budgets and cost metering run for real.

The default reply is `fixture: ` plus the first 60 characters of the last user message. A rules file scripts the rest: the first rule whose `match` is a substring of the system prompt or the last user message wins. This is how the demo kiosk tells its agents apart.

```json
[
  {"match": "refund", "reply": "Refund issued."},
  {"match": "weather", "tool": {"name": "get_weather", "args": {"city": "Austin"}}}
]
```

A `tool` rule fires only when the request declares tools. When the next request carries the tool result, the reply is `fixture: tool result: <first 60 chars>`, so a scripted tool loop always ends.

```bash
cd services/control-plane
go run ./cmd/llm-replay -rules rules.json      # 127.0.0.1:9192

PAL_LLM_BASEURL_OPENAI=http://127.0.0.1:9192 \
PAL_LLM_BASEURL_ANTHROPIC=http://127.0.0.1:9192 \
OPENAI_API_KEY=dummy make run-api

curl -s localhost:8080/v1/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hello"}]}'   # "fixture: hello"
curl -s 127.0.0.1:9192/__requests                         # what the control plane sent
```

- Dev and test only. The control plane refuses to start with either variable set when `PAL_ENV` is `prod`, `production` or `staging`, and ignores them at request time.
- A provider key must still exist (database or `OPENAI_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`); any dummy value works.
- Only `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages` are served. Embeddings, speech and transcription return 404.
- It echoes and follows rules. It has no model quality and cannot validate prompts.

## Example suites on a fixture stack

`make test-e2e-examples` runs `scripts/e2e-examples.sh`. It creates a throwaway database, starts `llm-replay`, `connector-replay` ([Connectors](/docs/build/connectors/)), the control plane (pointed at both) and the surface gateway, runs `e2e/examples`, and tears everything down. It never touches `:8080` or your dev database. It needs Postgres and Redis from `make dev-infra` (a random Redis DB 1 to 14 is used).

| Test | Flow |
| --- | --- |
| `TestDigest_*` | A schedule with `America/New_York` returns a 09:00 New York `nextFireAt`. Made due, the scheduler creates the run; GitHub is read and exactly one multi-line `chat.postMessage` reaches the Slack fixture with the digest intact; the schedule advances to the next 09:00. A bad timezone is a 400. |
| `TestTelegram_*` | A missing or wrong `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token` is a 401 and sends nothing. A signed update runs the workflow (Google Calendar fixture read) and a `sendMessage` with the answer reaches the Telegram fixture for the right chat; a second message gets its own reply. WhatsApp `X-Hub-Signature-256` negatives live in `services/surface-gateway/tests`. |
| `TestVoice_*` | Unsigned and wrong-token webhooks and status callbacks are 403 and change nothing. A signed inbound call gets TwiML and reserves $0.05 in `agent_usage_daily`; the status callback (61 s) reconciles it to $0.06, replays are no-ops, and a never-connected call refunds to zero. Over a hard-fail budget the call gets `<Reject/>` with no row and no spend. |

```bash
make dev-infra
make test-e2e-examples                 # ~70 s, mostly the scheduler's 60 s poll

E2E_EXAMPLES_SERVE=1 scripts/e2e-examples.sh   # leave the stack up, no tests (debugging)
scripts/e2e-examples.sh -run TestVoice          # extra args go to go test
```

- Connector and LLM replies are recorded fixtures. This proves the wiring and the security gates, not model quality or vendor API drift. Real-account runs are in each example's README.
- The gateway creates runs over gRPC, which the control plane's recovery sweep drives. The script sets `PAL_RECOVERY_INTERVAL=2s` so a reply takes seconds, not up to 30.
- It needs `go`, `cargo`, `psql`/`createdb` and `python3` on the PATH.

## Browser tier

`apps/web/e2e` drives the real dashboard in headless Chromium with Playwright: sign-up, forgot and reset password (the reset link is read from the log mailer), onboarding (template gallery and the free-text path through the fixture LLM to a succeeded first run), the settings danger zone, and the light and dark theme.

```bash
cd apps/web
npm ci && npx playwright install chromium
npm run test:e2e
```

It boots its own stack on spare ports (web 3411, API 8411, llm-replay 9412): a throwaway Postgres database, a private Redis db index, the control plane (with `PAL_CORS_ORIGINS` set to the dashboard origin), llm-replay and `next dev`. It never touches `:8080`, `:3001` or the shared dev database, and tears everything down afterwards. It needs Go, `psql`, and reachable Postgres and Redis (the `make dev-infra` defaults work; override with `E2E_PG_ADMIN_URL`, `E2E_REDIS_*`). Details: `apps/web/e2e/README.md`.

## CI

`.github/workflows/sdlc-e2e.yml` runs the fixture tier on every pull request and push to master, with Postgres (pgvector) and Redis service containers and no provider key. Three jobs: `examples` (`scripts/e2e-examples.sh`), `browser` (Playwright; report and traces upload on failure) and `deploy-cli` (`e2e/deploy` against a control plane started in the job). A skipped test fails the job. The real-LLM suites (`make test-e2e-llm`) are a local gate only, because they need a provider key and spend money.

## Not covered

- True cross-tenant isolation (a second tenant probing the first) needs a second seeded tenant.
- `PUT /v1/runtime/quota` clamps non-positive ceilings, so the 402 test pins `maxConcurrentVms` to the current live-VM count instead.
